title: What's Happening At Freedom Park? Bengaluru's Key Protest Space Closed | Bengaluru-news News - News18
text: Freedom Park, Bengaluru’s most recognisable public space for protests and civic movements, has been temporarily closed to facilitate infrastructure development. The decision has affected activists, daily walkers, and citizens who regularly use the 22-acre park for public gatherings, demonstrations, and peaceful assemblies. The closure came into effect this week, with public access blocked from inside the park. As a result, protesters who would usually hold demonstrations within Freedom Park have been forced to assemble outside its gates, leading to fresh confusion around permissions and crowd management. Why Freedom Park Has Been Closed Authorities say the closure is linked to ongoing development work being undertaken by the Greater Bengaluru Authority as part of its Brand Bengaluru initiative. The aim is to upgrade basic facilities inside the park, particularly infrastructure meant to support those who use the space for protests. Officials have stated that the work includes construction of toilets and other essential amenities for protesters, walkers, and visitors. The project is estimated to cost around Rs 5 crore and is being fast-tracked to minimise disruption. Until the work is completed, the park has been shut entirely from the inside, with electricity supply cut and no water facilities available. Impact on Protesters and Activists Freedom Park has long been recognised as the designated protest zone in Bengaluru, where activists from across Karnataka travel to make representations to the government. With the park now inaccessible, protest activity has spilled onto surrounding roads and pavements. Authorities have reportedly asked the police to stop granting permissions for protests not only inside the park but also in the immediate exterior areas, at least for this week. This has led to concerns among civil rights groups, who argue that restricting both the park and its surroundings limits avenues for peaceful protest. Several groups have said they were not given clear alternative locations, leaving them uncertain about where demonstrations can legally be held during the closure. Walkers and Regular Visitors Affected The closure has not only impacted protesters. Freedom Park is also a popular walking and recreation space, especially for residents in the city centre. Regular walkers say the sudden restriction has disrupted daily routines. Some visitors said the park’s closure has forced them to shift to busier roads or smaller parks nearby, which are not always accessible or safe. For many, Freedom Park offered a rare open, secure space in a congested part of the city. What Authorities Are Saying Officials have maintained that the closure is temporary and aimed at improving facilities, not restricting public access in the long term. Once the work is completed, they say Freedom Park will reopen for multiple uses, including protests, walking, filming, and other public activities. The authorities argue that better infrastructure will lead to a more organised and humane protest environment, particularly for those who spend long hours at the park during demonstrations. However, no clear reopening timeline has been publicly announced yet, which has added to uncertainty among users. A Park With a Civic Legacy Freedom Park occupies the site of Bengaluru’s former central jail and has, over the years, become symbolic of democratic expression in the city. From farmers’ movements to student groups, it has served as a space where dissent is visible but regulated. Because of this legacy, even temporary closures tend to draw greater scrutiny compared to other public parks. Activists and citizen groups are now urging authorities to complete the development work quickly and communicate timelines clearly. Many say infrastructure upgrades are welcome, but prolonged closures risk eroding the park’s role as a civic space. There are also calls for interim arrangements, such as designated alternative protest zones, until Freedom Park reopens fully. What Happens Next For now, Freedom Park remains closed, with access restricted and protest permissions curtailed. The coming days will be crucial in determining how quickly the development work progresses and whether authorities provide clarity on reopening. Until then, Bengaluru’s primary protest space remains out of bounds, leaving activists, walkers, and civil society groups waiting for the city’s most symbolic public park to open its gates again.
